kitDescription: Sakura is a Burst I Fire Supporter whose value is almost entirely team support rather than personal damage. Her Skill 1 grants all allies a stacking DEF buff (Cherry Blossom Tea, 8.15% of DEF, up to 10 stacks, 15s) after every 3 of her normal attacks — defensive in nature, but the stack count gates one of her burst lines. Her Skill 2 lets allies deal extra damage to enemy projectiles (relevant only in Anomaly-style fights) and, on every Full Burst entry, refunds 4.84 seconds of burst cooldown to all allies, accelerating the whole team's rotation. Her Burst reduces the damage the team takes from Wind-code enemies once per battle, grants all allies a flat ATK bonus equal to 23.76% of her own ATK for 10 seconds on every cast, and — only when Cherry Blossom Tea is at max stacks — boosts the team's damage to interruption parts for 30 seconds. In a single-boss damage sim with no incoming damage, no projectiles, and no parts, only the cooldown refund and the caster-scaled ATK buff move damage.

verdictRationale: No real gotchas. All six kit lines are either FAITHFUL (K1 Tea stack buff, K3 burstCdr, K5 caster-scaled ATK) or DOCUMENTED_GAP (K2 projectile, K4 wind mitigation, K6 gated parts) with verbatim unmodeled records and zero-leak assertions. The blind re-derivations converged strongly: S6's override is block-for-block identical on all four modeled/unmodeled structural decisions except K6, where S6's ungated-inert block is damage-identical to the driver's unmodeled verbatim and S6's own caveat concedes the gate cannot be enforced — a documentation-style divergence, not a finding. The 5 S5 REDs are a blind-fixture artifact (FB count in a liter-dominated comp is too coarse an observable for a 4.84s refund that crosses no count boundary in 180s); the blind's own run data corroborates the CDR is live (team damage delta, all-allies targeting), and the driver's sole-B1 cycle-length instrument discriminates the oncePerBattle nearest-wrong cleanly — RECON_ERROR-class, attributed to the blind, not the driver. Discrimination holds on every load-bearing driver test (K1 stat + trigger counterfactuals, K3 oncePerBattle, K5 atkPct, K6 add-parts byte-equality). Same-model residual the owner should spot-check: the refresh-vs-expiry stack semantics of Cherry Blossom Tea are kit-silent and currently unobservable (defPct inert) — if DEF ever feeds damage or the K6 gate gains a primitive, the 15s/stack-refresh question becomes live and needs a measurement, not an assumption; secondarily, whether max stacks are ever reachable at real SR cadence (driver/S5 both estimate ~3–4 stacks steady state under non-refresh) remains unmeasured and only matters if parts damage ever becomes live.
